extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news editors, media critics, and students of press criticism
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric for newsroom story selection and framing based on Jay Rosen's PressThink: prioritize democratic utility and citizens' needs over insider-driven metrics. It provides tests and anti-patterns for editors to decide what to cover and how to frame it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic utility as newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness must be earned by demonstrated democratic utility — stories should be judged by the public good they serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient story selection toward what contributes to democratic life (informed voting, accountability, public decision-making) rather than what maximizes attention or satisfies insiders. This is the overarching principle of Rosen's rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizens Agenda approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with what voters say they need to know to cast a vote; demote what insiders find interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience surveys and listening to set priorities. Prioritize topics and angles that answer citizens' practical needs rather than reporting that reflects elite interests or newsroom peer-preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymmetry test
rubrics_metrics.description: "Both sides" framing fails when one side breaks norms more; newsworthiness criteria must update when reality is asymmetric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When actors are not symmetrical in behavior or threat (e.g., one side repeatedly breaks norms, lies, or poses danger), avoid automatic parity in coverage. Update balance norms to reflect asymmetric realities rather than defaulting to formulaic evenhandedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware coverage that lets the press appear neutral while taking sides by omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether omitting certain facts or lines of inquiry produces an appearance of neutrality while effectively siding with powerful actors. Newsworthy items are those a press accountable to citizens — not insiders — would cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: View from nowhere critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional neutrality that hides ideological choices (the "view from nowhere") is deceptive; a defended news judgment is preferable to a hidden one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about editorial reasoning where appropriate. Reject faux-objectivity that obscures values or choices; better to show and defend the standards guiding coverage than to pretend there are none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability vs. access test
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this story serving accountability or access?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reporting that holds power to account over stories that primarily maintain or cultivate access to elites. Use this as a quick litmus test when deciding whether to run or pursue a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda-setting check
rubrics_metrics.description: Did we let the powerful set the agenda this week?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodically evaluate whether coverage priorities are being set by powerful actors, PR cycles, or insiders. If so, reset to focus on citizens' concerns and issues of democratic consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover citizens' needs rather than elites' wants
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask whether coverage reflects what citizens need covered or what elites/insiders want covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in tension, prioritize issues (e.g., jobs, healthcare, schools) that affect citizens' daily lives and civic decisions, even if elites deem them less newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro-democracy framing test
rubrics_metrics.description: Is our framing pro-democracy or pseudo-balanced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between genuine attempts to inform civic decision-making and fake balance that obscures threats to democratic processes. Favor frames that illuminate democratic stakes rather than neutral-sounding frames that hide harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote process/horse-race/palace-intrigue coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: De-emphasize process-oriented or horse-race reporting that focuses on tactics, insider maneuvering, or palace intrigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such coverage often serves insiders and entertains rather than informing citizens' democratic choices. Reduce prominence of these pieces in favor of substantive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stenography of partisan claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not act as a stenographer for partisan assertions without verification or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should not mechanically reproduce partisan talking points. Verify claims, provide context, and assess their relevance to citizens' understanding rather than amplifying raw partisan rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject 'both-sides' treatment of factual disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid false equivalence in factual disputes where evidence favors one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disputes are about facts rather than opinion, weight coverage according to evidence rather than forcing symmetry. Treat proven facts and debunked claims appropriately rather than presenting them as equal arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate stakes journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize journalism that highlights significant stakes and consequences for citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give prominence to reporting that clarifies what is at risk for public life, policy, or civic participation. 'Stakes' stories help citizens make informed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate citizen-agenda topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Give increased attention to topics on the citizen agenda (e.g., jobs, healthcare, schools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly boost coverage of everyday policy areas that most affect voters' lives, even if they are not sensational or elite-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-first coverage even when partisan-coded
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize factual reporting even if the facts align with or are coded as partisan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not shy away from fact-forward stories because they may benefit one side rhetorically; accuracy and public understanding trump perceived partisan optics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication accountability of the press
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the press accountable to citizens by subjecting stories and editorial choices to pre-publication scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include internal checks and public-facing justifications for significant editorial decisions; anticipate and test whether coverage serves democratic needs rather than insider interests.
